title: RouteWeaver rewrite: declarative routing transpiler and schema safeguard
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: The current routing rule evaluator mixes parsing, validation, and runtime decision logic which makes it brittle to schema changes, hard to test for backcompat, and risky to extend for region/tier/fallback requirements. We see repeated hotfixes when customers modify routing DSL (region selectors, tier weights, fallback model variants) and subtle behavior differences between the validator and the runtime interpreter.

Proposal: Implement a new "RouteWeaver" transpiler and schema safeguard layer that canonicalizes routing configs into a compact Intermediate Representation (IR) at config write time and provides a deterministic validation pipeline. The transpiler will: 1) parse declarative DSL into a strongly-typed canonical IR, 2) run a staged validator (linting, constraint checks, semantic compatibility), 3) emit transformation artifacts (compat shims for older fields, migration hints), and 4) produce a runtime-compatible contract that the serving runtime consumes. This separates concerns, improves testability, and enables safe progressive rollout with feature flags.

Goals: reduce config-related incidents, make DSL changes safe and observable, provide clear migration messages to customers and SREs, and preserve deterministic runtime behavior across versions.
acceptance_criteria: RouteWeaver library parses the complete routing DSL (region selectors, tier routing, fallback variants, weights) to a canonical IR with unit test coverage >= 90%
Staged validator emits user-facing error messages with actionable remediation for at least 95% of common misconfigs (missing region, ambiguous tier weights, invalid fallback type)
Runtime compatibility layer accepts the transpiled contract and produces identical routing decisions to the current runtime for the existing rule corpus (golden corpus regression test)
A gradual migration mode exists behind a config feature flag allowing coexistence of old evaluator and RouteWeaver-transpiled contracts
Automated migration job detects and reports incompatible configs and provides auto-fix suggestions in the console UI
migration_plan: Stage 0: Create RouteWeaver repo and core parser module. Write grammar and initial IR definitions.
Stage 1: Implement staged validator (lint -> schema -> semantic). Add clear error codes and remediation hints.
Stage 2: Build compatibility shim generator to translate legacy fields into canonical IR for the golden corpus.
Stage 3: Integrate transpiler into config-service behind 'routeweaver_enabled' feature flag and add telemetry for validation failures.
Stage 4: Run compatibility tests across historical configs and deploy canary with 1% of traffic using transpiled contracts.
Stage 5: Expand canary to 10/25/50% observing routing_mismatch_rate and error trends; roll to 100% when metrics stable.
Stage 6: Deprecate old evaluator after 4 weeks of stable operation and remove feature flag in follow-up cleanup PRs.
testing_plan: Unit tests for parser/generation covering edge cases for region selectors, tier priorities, and fallback variant chaining
Property-based fuzzing to discover ambiguous grammar constructs and ensure deterministic parse trees
Golden-corpus regression harness comparing RouteWeaver output vs current evaluator across 10k real configs
Integration test in staging with synthetic traffic exercising regional failover and tiered capacity fallbacks
E2E test with Console UI validation messages surfaced in the config editor and migration suggestion flow
rollout_plan: Deploy RouteWeaver library as a separate binary behind feature flag in config service
Enable validation-only mode for all configs for 48h to collect validation noise (no runtime effect)
Canary: enable transpile+serve for internal non-production orgs (1% traffic) for 72h
Gradually increase canary to 10% and 25% while monitoring routing_mismatch_rate <= 0.1% and p95 latency regression < 5ms
If issues detected, revert to validation-only mode, triage errors, and apply fixes to transpiler/compat-shims
Complete migration for all traffic and remove legacy evaluator after stability window
risks: False positives/negatives in validator causing user-facing rejections or silent misrouting
Performance regression in config evaluation path adding latency to request routing decisions
Compatibility gaps for rare legacy config patterns leading to different runtime behavior
Operational complexity during rollback if feature flag orchestration is not robust
